root_cause.description: Base-mint raw units were incorrectly cast to Lamports type, then displayed as SOL without conversion.
defect_explanation: calculate_net_profit_raw() returns net profit in BASE MINT RAW UNITS (e.g., USDC raw units, 6 decimals).
The return value was wrapped in `Lamports()` type, falsely implying SOL lamports (9 decimals).
profit_sol = real_net_profit.as_u64() / scale divided by base_decimals scale (10^6 for USDC) but labeled as 'SOL'.
roi_pct = real_net_profit / size_in * 100 compared base-mint raw with input raw — mathematically valid only for same-mint, but misleadingly labeled as '% ROI'.
initial_loan_sol = size_in / 1e9 divided by SOL decimals (1e9) even though size_in may be USDC raw units (6 decimals).

reproduction.correct_roi: roi_pct = 32,985,083 / 3,415,629 * 100 = 965.7% (valid for same-mint ratio, but misleading label)

root_cause.impact: All profit/ROI displays are denominationaly incorrect when base_mint is not SOL. ROI anomaly is a display/labeling error, not an actual 965% return.

changes: Removed `Lamports(real_net_raw)` cast — value stays in base mint raw units.
Min profit floor converted from lamports to base mint raw units using verified rate before comparison.
Profit displayed using base mint decimals scale, not hardcoded 1e9.
SOL-denominated display uses `base_raw_to_lamports_checked()` with verified rate.
ROI calculation uses same-mint raw units (base mint raw / input raw).
All info! macro labels use `opp.base_mint` instead of hardcoded 'SOL'.

secondary_defect.description: When `fresh_pools` is empty after slot-window filtering, ALL active pools (including stale ones) are retained, bypassing freshness validation.
secondary_defect.fix: Replaced with fail-closed `continue` — no stale pool may enter a candidate route.
